subject: HealthIQ trial: success metrics, owner alignment, and exec decision slot
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@healthiq.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: HealthIQ trial: proposed POC scope and success metrics

Hi Maya / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before we circulate a formal POC plan. I put the detailed plan in the attached doc (20271102-healthisiq-poc-plan.docx) and SOC 2 answers in the PDF.

POC overview (proposed)
- Length: 3 weeks (sandbox) + 1 week validation with sample production traffic
- Primary goals: reduce content-classification latency for high-volume flows; improve entity extraction precision on claims data; verify end-to-end throughput at 250 TPS for 512-token windows

Success metrics (pass/fail):
- 95th percentile latency < 220 ms for 1–2k token requests
- Entity extraction F1 >= 0.87 on agreed evaluation set
- Error rate < 0.5% (server/HTTP errors)
- No PII leakage in audit logs; retention behavior confirmed by Legal

Evaluation plan and ownership
- Redwood: runtime provisioning, workload mirroring, performance monitoring, and trace access (owner: Sean)
- HealthIQ Dev: supply evaluation dataset, run closed-loop accuracy checks, and validate predictions (owner: Maya)
- Customer Ops/CS: define acceptance gating and hit the go/no-go checklist at trial end (owner: Monica)

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (alignment): finalize test dataset + legal scoping (this week)
- Weeks 1–3: POC runs + daily syncs (M/W/F 30m)
- Week 4: validation pass and final exec readout (30 minutes)

Exec decision slot 
- Can you confirm an executive readout window? Proposed dates: Nov 15 (Tue) 10:00–10:30 ET or Nov 16 (Wed) 11:00–11:30 ET. We’ll use that call for a go/no-go and to align on next-contract steps.

Immediate asks
1) Confirm the success metrics above or list any changes.
2) Confirm owners for the evaluation items and Legal contact for retention questions.
3) Pick the preferred exec readout slot or suggest alternatives.

Attachments: 20271102-healthisiq-poc-plan.docx, healthiq-soc2-answers.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with an updated mutual action plan once I hear back.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@healthiq.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@healthiq.com>, Legal Contracts <legal@healthiq.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HealthIQ trial: proposed POC scope and success metrics

Thanks Sean — this is very helpful. Quick notes from our side:

- The metrics look good overall. We do want to tighten the entity extraction F1 target to 0.90 for the high-priority claims subset (we can accept 0.87 across the full dataset but want 0.90 on top 20% of cases).
- Please add our Legal contact (copied) for retention and audit-log requirements — Legal will need to confirm the retention window and the exact log fields we can access during the trial.
- Exec slot: Nov 16 (Wed) 11:00–11:30 ET works best for our Director + Head of Product. If you can pencil that, we’ll confirm internally and lock in.

Also: can you confirm whether the sandbox will include prefix/KV cache enabled? That matters for latency measurements.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Data Platforms, HealthIQ
maya.singh@healthiq.com | +1 917-555-2219

Date: 2027-11-04T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HealthIQ trial: proposed POC scope and success metrics

Looping in internal owners and next ops steps.

Internal owners (confirmed)
- Trials & Provisioning: Monica Patel (CS) — set up sandbox, sample traffic mirroring, and health checks
- SRE/Runtime: Sean Gallagher — kernel selection, batching config, and monitoring hooks
- Account Exec / Contract: Aditya Rao — pricing path & commercial terms
- Program Manager: Lauren Bishop — daily sync cadence and MOPs checklist
CS asks before trial start
1) Access plan for HealthIQ engineers to push test vectors (S3 link + temporary keys).
2) Decision gate: if 95th pctl latency during Week 2 is > 300 ms, we’ll pause and triage (fail-for-retry).
Go/no-go checklist (short)
- Data ingestion validated by HealthIQ (owner: Maya)
- Performance pass (95th pctl < 220 ms)
- Accuracy gating met for top claims subset (F1 >= 0.90)
Aditya — can you provision trial credits and confirm estimated monthly run rate if they convert at the projected volume? Need a quick sketch to include in the exec pack.
I’ll prepare the 1-pager acceptance checklist and update the mutual action plan after we lock the exec date.
—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

- If trial passes the acceptance checklist, we are prepared to offer a 12-month committed plan with a 10% onboarding credit (subject to standard sales approval).

Estimate ask: Sean / Monica — can you share an expected monthly token estimate for the projected 250 TPS sustained window so I can sketch ARR implications? I’ll include that in the exec pack.
